rows.name: Merck & Co.
rows.thesis: A defensive large drugmaker with low volatility (34%) and a 4.3% free-cash-flow yield, 4.6 points ahead of the ETF since purchase; health care is one of the sectors holding up in this correction.
rows.risks: The GAAP P/E of 143 includes one-off charges, and a pipeline or patent setback would hit the earnings path.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 8.4% above), or a pipeline or patent setback breaks the earnings path.

rows.name: Targa Resources
rows.thesis: Fee-based gas gathering and processing that grows with Permian volumes; it fell only 5% in a month when energy fell 11%, and it is now my only energy name, 4 points ahead of the ETF.
rows.risks: Lower oil prices from Middle East peace talks could slow Permian drilling and volumes, and net debt is 31% of market value.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 6.4% above), or management cuts its volume guidance.

rows.name: Nucor
rows.thesis: The leading US steelmaker behind tariff protection: 22% revenue growth, a P/E of 15.8, a 4.8% free-cash-flow yield and a solid balance sheet, 1.7 points ahead of the ETF; trimmed slightly to match medium conviction.
rows.risks: A recession scare or looser steel tariffs would hit steel prices, and it is my whole materials overweight.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 7.3% above), or tariff policy on steel is loosened.

rows.name: DuPont
rows.thesis: The slimmer post-breakup DuPont keeps rising in a falling market (+11.7% over a month, 2% under its high) and is 25 points ahead of the ETF since purchase, with a 3.9% free-cash-flow yield.
rows.risks: Its GAAP P/E of 75 (breakup charges included) leaves little room if the re-rating stalls.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 9.7% above), or its lead over the S&P 500 ETF since purchase falls below +5 points.

rows.name: CrowdStrike
rows.thesis: Big move, kept as an overreaction: Q3 (reported November 23) was strong (revenue +28% to $1.58 billion, record net new annual recurring revenue of $419 million, guidance raised). The roughly 9% drop that day came from the $43.9 billion all-stock Zscaler deal, not the business, and the share is still 15.7% above its 200-day average.
rows.risks: The Zscaler deal dilutes existing holders and adds integration risk, and at 77% volatility the share swings with the tech selloff.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or the Zscaler integration points to sharply slower recurring-revenue growth.

rows.name: Hasbro
rows.thesis: Growing (+19% revenue) and profitable (18% margin), with a 7.9% free-cash-flow yield at a P/E of 16.5; my steadiest share (25% volatility), 17% above its 200-day average.
rows.risks: It fell 6.8% this week for a reason I could not confirm, and its Q4 depends on holiday toy demand and the digital gaming segment.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 16.8% above), or Q4 results show the digital gaming segment slowing sharply.

rows.name: Viatris
rows.thesis: A cheap generic-drug maker paying down debt, with a 9.3% free-cash-flow yield; up 6% over a month in a falling market and 15 points ahead of the ETF since purchase.
rows.risks: Net debt is 51% of market value and GAAP earnings are negative, so any setback in debt reduction would hurt.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 20% above), or debt reduction stalls.

rows.name: Marathon Petroleum
rows.thesis: My only refiner: P/E of 7.2, 21% free-cash-flow yield and heavy buybacks, still 19.5% above its 200-day average.
rows.risks: Refining margins are volatile, and the share is down 20% over a month.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 25 points since purchase.

rows.name: Target Corporation
rows.thesis: Q3 beat with raised full-year guidance; up 16% over a month, 2% under its high, at a P/E of 16 with a 5.3% free-cash-flow yield; it fills my staples weight and is 4 points ahead of the ETF since purchase.
rows.risks: Part of the guidance raise came from one-off tariff refunds, and holiday sales could disappoint.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 23.6% above), or holiday sales trends reverse the raised guidance.

rows.name: NetApp
rows.thesis: Storage for AI data at a P/E of 23, with a 5.1% free-cash-flow yield and net cash; held into Q2 results after the close on December 1 (confirmed), against guidance of $2.025-2.175 billion in revenue.
rows.risks: The AI-hardware selloff plus any results miss could push it through its 200-day average (now 4.3% above).
rows.exit_if: Q2 revenue or guidance disappoints, or it closes more than 3% under its 200-day average.

rows.name: Keysight Technologies
rows.thesis: Record fiscal Q4 on November 19 (revenue +41%, orders +53%) shows AI and networking test demand is strong; the 20% monthly fall tracks the AI-hardware selloff, not its business.
rows.risks: As an AI-hardware supplier it keeps falling with the chip complex (75% volatility, 17% under its 200-day average).
rows.exit_if: It falls more than 25% below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 20 points since purchase (now 13.6), or a fiscal 2027 outlook implies growth below 10%.

rows.name: Morgan Stanley
rows.thesis: Wealth-management fees and capital markets at a P/E of 13.3, with 16% revenue growth and a 25.5% margin; level with the ETF since purchase (+0.4 points).
rows.risks: It is 14.1% under its 200-day average, just above my exit line, and a falling market cuts deal and asset-based fees.
rows.exit_if: It falls more than 15% below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 10 points since purchase.

rows.name: Illumina, Inc.
rows.thesis: Q3 beat with raised guidance, a 20% net margin and net cash; still 9% above its 200-day average, so the 29% monthly fall looks like the unwind of high-momentum shares, though I could not confirm a cause.
rows.risks: Revenue growth is only 5.8% at a P/E of 34.5, and an unexplained drop while health care rose could hide a company-specific problem.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 25 points since purchase (now 17).

rows.name: Omnicom Group
rows.thesis: Organic growth accelerated to 7.2% in Q3 as Interpublic synergies arrive; it has an 11.6% free-cash-flow yield and net cash, is at its 52-week high and up 14.8% over a month, and it is my only communication-services name in a sector where I am 5 points under the index.
rows.risks: Its GAAP margin of 2.8% reflects merger costs, and ad budgets would shrink if the selloff turns into a recession scare.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 14.3% above), or organic growth falls back below 3%.
